content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text decides a clash involving the challenger's footed chain and then cites Matthew 1:20's own words as the counter, which is the verse-by-verse move K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse: one reading is that the judge may not isolate Matthew 1:20's own words to answer the challenger's chain; the other reading is that a single verse's explicit wording may be used as part of chain weighing.", "why": "Because the judge says the challenger's analogy is footed but then rests the clash on the sentence's own words, it uses a single verse's wording instead of weighing chain against chain by footing."}
